summary: Dog Mountain, Lake County, Oregon: 1926 cupola and 1947 cabin replaced by a 1997 two-story live-in cab; drive-up with no gate; staffing reports conflict.

facts.design: two-story live-in cab built 1997 (about 15 by 15 feet); earlier L-4 cabin of 1947

staffing.status: staffed every summer per one source; locked for the season on a June 2022 visit

access.note: Drive-up forest road with no gate; a June 2022 visitor drove to the summit. The cab is in active service and was locked on that visit, so entry should not be expected.

visit.trail_note: Gravel route via Dog Lake Lane and NF-406, about 5.5 miles from the NF-085 junction to the summit; a 2022 trip report calls the road exposed and narrow. Check with the Lakeview Ranger District before a visit.

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Fremont-Winema National Forest (Lakeview Ranger District)

corrections.proposed: two-story live-in cab (1997); L-4 cabin applies to the 1947 structure that was replaced
corrections.why: The L-4 cabin was built in 1947 and replaced in 1997 by a two-story cab. The record's L-4 describes the earlier structure, not the one standing now.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and Rex's page call the 1947 house an L-4 cabin. Forest Lookouts calls it a 14 by 14 Aladdin-style house. Both are reported; the record does not settle it.
The register gives 6,890 feet (2,100 m) and Rex's page gives 6,936 feet. Both are reported in the story; there is no elevation fact key.
The register gives 15 by 15 feet for the two-story cab; Forest Lookouts gives 15 feet 4 inches a side. Both are reported.
Rex's page says staffed every summer (undated). A June 2022 visitor found the lookout locked for the season. Both are reported; current staffing is not confirmed.

notes_for_editor: Brief's design L-4 describes the 1947 cabin, not the cab standing now (two-story, 1997); corrected. Staffing is contested: Rex's page says staffed every summer (undated), while the June 2022 visit found it locked for the season and no one present. Cab size (15 by 15 vs 15 feet 4 inches) and elevation (6,890 vs 6,936 feet) conflict across sources and are both reported. The 1947 structure type conflicts too (L-4 vs Aladdin-style 14 by 14). The 1995 proposal and 1997 build details come from Forest Lookouts quoting Forest Service archive text; not read in the original. Lookout history of Bertha Covert (1918) is from the register; the 1919 and 1920 newspaper item was not used. No photos added; the register and Rex's page carry photo credits that were not checked for license. Fact-check 2026-10-08: the 1956 and 1960 Malin items are cited to Forest Lookouts' Herald and News quotes; 'locked up' is now the 2022 visitor's own report that it seemed locked; 6,890 and 6,936 feet are elevations, not summit claims.
